publication: New-York Daily Tribune (NEW JERSEY NEWS page)
summary: Page 14 profile, 'A Noted Colored Leader: Sketch of R. Henri Herbert, of Mercer County,' describes Herbert as the political organizer who unified Black Republican voters across Mercer County and New Jersey behind Gov. John W. Griggs. Born in Trenton in 1857, Herbert worked in newspapers from boyhood: business manager of The New-Jersey State Republican (Plainfield), editorial writer/reporter for The Daily State Sentinel and The Daily Free Press (Trenton), and founder in 1880 of The Weekly Sentinel, which he ran three years before selling it to Colonel E. C. Stahl, who merged it into The Trenton Herald. In 1884-85 Herbert served as NJ Commissioner of Colored Exhibits at the New Orleans Exposition, then returned to Trenton to manufacture cigars. His father, Mansfield Herbert, was born enslaved near Washington, escaped at 14, settled in South Trenton, and before age 30 purchased freedom for himself, his father, and his sister for over $3,000; from 1843 until the Civil War his house was a principal Underground Railroad station between Philadelphia and New Brunswick. The same page also carries unrelated NJ political profiles (Rutherford's Union Club fire, Bloomfield's old Presbyterian church centenary, Thomas Dunn English sketch) and general news items.
